current_law_statement: Researched 2026-08-19 against the codified Texas Government Code ch. 552 (Public Information Act) as served by the Legislative Council (statutes.capitol.texas.gov / tcss.legis.texas.gov), current through the 89th Legislature Regular Session and 2nd Called Session (2025) — the chapter text carries 2025 amendment notes (e.g., § 552.221 by H.B. 4219, § 552.234 by H.B. 4214, eff. 2025). Subchapter F (§§ 552.261-.275, charges) was last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033) (§§ 552.271, 552.272, 552.275); no 2024-2026 session law touched the fee/estimate/deposit sections. The delegated instrument, 1 Tex. Admin. Code ch. 70 (Office of the Attorney General cost rules, §§ 70.1-70.13), was opened on the Secretary of State's TAC portal (texas-sos.appianportalsgov.com; the old texreg.sos.state.tx.us viewer now redirects there) with source notes: § 70.3 and § 70.7 last amended effective Feb. 22, 2007 (32 TexReg 614); § 70.12 adopted Sept. 5, 2007; § 70.13 (body-worn camera fee) adopted Nov. 24, 2016. The AG's 2026 Public Information Act Handbook (opened) reproduces ch. 70 identically and adds two guidance-only points used here: the 50% deposit cap is limited to paper-inspection requests, and 'decisions about method of payment rest with the governmental body'. Guidance-vs-law gap: 1 TAC § 70.7(d) phrases the deposit trigger as '$100 or more / $50 or more' while § 552.263(a) says 'exceed' — statute governs. The 2026 Texas Legislature does not meet in regular session; no pending fee amendments were identified.

resolutions.source_authority: 1 Tex. Admin. Code § 70.3(b)(1); Tex. Gov't Code § 552.262(a)
resolutions.source_language: (1) Standard paper copy. The charge for standard paper copies reproduced by means of an office machine copier or a computer printer is $.10 per page or part of a page. Each side that has recorded information is considered a page. [§ 552.262(a):] The charges for providing copies of public information may not be excessive and may not exceed the actual cost of producing the information or for making public information that exists in a paper record available for inspection. A governmental body, other than an agency of state government, may determine its own charges for providing copies of public information and its own charge, deposit, or bond for making public information that exists in a paper record available for inspection but may not charge an amount that is greater than 25 percent more than the amount established by the attorney general unless the governmental body requests an exemption under Subsection (c).
resolutions.effective_status: Current (1 TAC § 70.3 last amended effective February 22, 2007, 32 TexReg 614; verified on the SOS TAC portal as of 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: Delegation followed: § 552.262 → 1 TAC § 70.3(b)(1) opened on the SOS TAC portal (last amended eff. Feb. 22, 2007). Municipal regime: § 552.262(a) lets a governmental body other than a state agency set its own charge up to 25 percent above the AG-established amount without an exemption (1 TAC § 70.1(b)(2), § 70.4(c)); state agencies must use the AG amount. Charges may never exceed actual cost. Cities holding an AG exemption (published annually in the Texas Register) may differ. $0.125 is arithmetic (0.10 × 1.25), not a printed figure. For 50-or-fewer-page paper requests the per-page charge is the ONLY charge (TX-0026).

[§ 70.3(b)(1):] The charge for standard paper copies reproduced by means of an office machine copier or a computer printer is $.10 per page or part of a page.

new_rules.legal_concept: AG-established standard paper copy charge
new_rules.atomic_rule: The charge for a standard paper copy reproduced by office copier or computer printer is $.10 per page or part of a page; each side with recorded information is a page (AG-established amount; non-state bodies may exceed it by up to 25% without an exemption).
new_rules.trigger: Requestor asks for standard paper copies (up to 8 1/2 x 14 in.).
new_rules.source_language: (1) Standard paper copy. The charge for standard paper copies reproduced by means of an office machine copier or a computer printer is $.10 per page or part of a page. Each side that has recorded information is considered a page.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (1 TAC § 70.3 last amended effective February 22, 2007, 32 TexReg 614; verified on the SOS TAC portal as of 2026-08-19)
new_rules.notes: Instrument delegated by Gov't Code § 552.262(a)-(b). For municipalities the AG figure is a baseline: § 552.262(a) lets a governmental body other than a state agency set its own charge up to 25% above the AG amount ($.125/page) without an exemption; higher requires an AG exemption under 1 TAC § 70.4. No separate color-copy rate exists in ch. 70; a color impression on standard-size paper falls within the 'standard paper copy' definition of § 70.2(9).

new_rules.legal_concept: Charges capped at actual cost; non-state bodies may exceed AG amounts by no more than 25%
new_rules.atomic_rule: Charges for copies may not be excessive and may not exceed the actual cost of producing the information; a governmental body other than a state agency may set its own charges but may not charge more than 25 percent above the AG-established amount unless it obtains an exemption.
new_rules.trigger: Body imposes a charge for copies or for paper inspection.
new_rules.source_language: The charges for providing copies of public information may not be excessive and may not exceed the actual cost of producing the information or for making public information that exists in a paper record available for inspection. A governmental body, other than an agency of state government, may determine its own charges for providing copies of public information and its own charge, deposit, or bond for making public information that exists in a paper record available for inspection but may not charge an amount that is greater than 25 percent more than the amount established by the attorney general unless the governmental body requests an exemption under Subsection (c).
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
new_rules.notes: AMENDS TX-0027: supplies the verbatim clause TX-0027 had only as a paraphrase and corrects its status to Current. § 552.262(c): exemption request in writing to AG; AG decides within 90 days.

new_rules.legal_concept: Deposit or bond for unpaid amounts on prior requests (> $100)
new_rules.atomic_rule: Before preparing a copy for a new request, the officer may require a deposit or bond for unpaid amounts owed on the requestor's previous requests if those unpaid amounts exceed $100, and may not seek payment of those amounts through any other means.
new_rules.trigger: Requestor owes more than $100 in unpaid amounts on previous requests under ch. 552.
new_rules.source_language: (c) An officer for public information or the officer's agent may require a deposit or bond for payment of unpaid amounts owing to the governmental body in relation to previous requests that the requestor has made under this chapter before preparing a copy of public information in response to a new request if those unpaid amounts exceed $100. The officer for public information or the officer's agent may not seek payment of those unpaid amounts through any other means.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
new_rules.notes: AMENDS TX-0035: the provision is § 552.263(c), not (a-1); verbatim text supplied. 1 TAC § 70.7(f)-(g) restates: applies where the body provided, and the requestor accepted, itemized statements that remain unpaid and the aggregated unpaid amount exceeds $100.

new_rules.legal_concept: Labor charge for locating, compiling, manipulating data and reproducing
new_rules.atomic_rule: The labor charge for processing a request is $15 an hour and covers the actual time to locate, compile, manipulate data, and reproduce the requested information (AG-established; +25% municipal variance).

new_rules.atomic_rule: A labor charge shall not be billed for requests for 50 or fewer pages of paper records unless the documents are located in two or more separate, unconnected buildings or in a remote storage facility; buildings joined by a sidewalk or passageway are not separate.
new_rules.trigger: Request is for 50 or fewer pages of paper records.
new_rules.source_language: (2) A labor charge shall not be billed in connection with complying with requests that are for 50 or fewer pages of paper records, unless the documents to be copied are located in: (A) Two or more separate buildings that are not physically connected with each other; or (B) A remote storage facility. [...] (6) For purposes of paragraph (2)(A) of this subsection, two buildings connected by a covered or open sidewalk, an elevated or underground passageway, or a similar facility, are not considered to be separate buildings.

new_rules.legal_concept: No labor charge for exception review or AG-ruling preparation
new_rules.atomic_rule: No labor charge may be recovered for time spent by an attorney, legal assistant or anyone else reviewing the information to decide whether to raise exceptions or to research/prepare a request for an AG ruling.
new_rules.trigger: Staff time is spent on exception review or preparing a § 552.301 ruling request.
new_rules.source_language: (3) A labor charge shall not be recovered for any time spent by an attorney, legal assistant, or any other person who reviews the requested information: (A) To determine whether the governmental body will raise any exceptions to disclosure of the requested information under the Texas Government Code, Subchapter C, Chapter 552; or (B) To research or prepare a request for a ruling by the attorney general's office pursuant to §552.301 of the Texas Government Code.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (1 TAC § 70.3 last amended effective February 22, 2007, 32 TexReg 614; verified on the SOS TAC portal as of 2026-08-19)
new_rules.notes: Distinguishes 'review' (never chargeable) from 'redaction' of confidential information (chargeable under (d)(4), TX-9011).

new_rules.legal_concept: Labor for redacting mandatorily confidential information
new_rules.atomic_rule: When confidential information under a mandatory exception is mixed with public information on the same page, labor may be recovered for time spent redacting it, but not for requests of 50 or fewer pages unless the request otherwise qualifies for a labor charge.
new_rules.trigger: Page mixes mandatorily confidential and public information and must be redacted before release.
new_rules.source_language: (4) When confidential information pursuant to a mandatory exception of the Act is mixed with public information in the same page, a labor charge may be recovered for time spent to redact, blackout, or otherwise obscure confidential information in order to release the public information. A labor charge shall not be made for redacting confidential information for requests of 50 or fewer pages, unless the request also qualifies for a labor charge pursuant to Texas Government Code, §552.261(a)(1) or (2).
new_rules.effective_status: Current (1 TAC § 70.3 last amended effective February 22, 2007, 32 TexReg 614; verified on the SOS TAC portal as of 2026-08-19)

new_rules.legal_concept: Programming labor rate
new_rules.atomic_rule: If a request requires a programmer to execute an existing program or create a new one to access and copy the information, the body may charge the programmer's time at $28.50 an hour; only programming services may be charged at that rate (AG-established; +25% municipal variance).
new_rules.trigger: Request requires programming to access and copy the information.
new_rules.source_language: (c) Labor charge for programming. If a particular request requires the services of a programmer in order to execute an existing program or to create a new program so that requested information may be accessed and copied, the governmental body may charge for the programmer's time. (1) The hourly charge for a programmer is $28.50 an hour. Only programming services shall be charged at this hourly rate. (2) Governmental bodies that do not have in-house programming capabilities shall comply with requests in accordance with §552.231 of the Texas Government Code.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (1 TAC § 70.3 last amended effective February 22, 2007, 32 TexReg 614; verified on the SOS TAC portal as of 2026-08-19)
new_rules.notes: Municipal ceiling absent exemption = $35.625/hr. Data 'manipulation' (non-programming) is billed at $15/hr under (d)(1).

new_rules.legal_concept: Overhead charge at 20% of labor
new_rules.atomic_rule: Whenever a labor charge applies, the body may add an overhead charge, which if recovered shall be computed at 20% of the labor charge; no overhead for requests of 50 or fewer pages of standard paper records unless the request qualifies for a labor charge.
new_rules.trigger: A labor charge (search/compile/reproduce or programming) applies to the request.
new_rules.source_language: (1) Whenever any labor charge is applicable to a request, a governmental body may include in the charges direct and indirect costs, in addition to the specific labor charge. This overhead charge would cover such costs as depreciation of capital assets, rent, maintenance and repair, utilities, and administrative overhead. If a governmental body chooses to recover such costs, a charge shall be made in accordance with the methodology described in paragraph (3) of this subsection. [...] (2) An overhead charge shall not be made for requests for copies of 50 or fewer pages of standard paper records unless the request also qualifies for a labor charge pursuant to Texas Government Code, §552.261(a)(1) or (2). (3) The overhead charge shall be computed at 20% of the charge made to cover any labor costs associated with a particular request.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (1 TAC § 70.3 last amended effective February 22, 2007, 32 TexReg 614; verified on the SOS TAC portal as of 2026-08-19)
new_rules.notes: Permission to recover; fixed methodology once elected. Whether the § 552.262(a) 25% variance can be applied to the 20% percentage is not addressed — flag. Overhead is not allowed on inspection requests (Gov't Code § 552.271(c),(d); § 552.272; Handbook 2026 at 53-54).

new_rules.legal_concept: Computer resource charge
new_rules.atomic_rule: A computer utilization charge may be recovered for actual CPU/clock time to execute a program: mainframe $10 per CPU minute; midsize $1.50 per CPU minute; client/server $2.20 per clock hour; PC or LAN $1.00 per clock hour; not for programming or printing time.
new_rules.trigger: Fulfilling the request requires computer execution of a program.
new_rules.source_language: Type of System--Rate: mainframe--$10 per CPU minute; Midsize--$1.50 per CPU minute; Client/Server--$2.20 per clock hour; PC or LAN--$1.00 per clock hour. (4) The charge made to recover the computer utilization cost is the actual time the computer takes to execute a particular program times the applicable rate. The CPU charge is not meant to apply to programming or printing time; rather it is solely to recover costs associated with the actual time required by the computer to execute a program.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (1 TAC § 70.3 last amended effective February 22, 2007, 32 TexReg 614; verified on the SOS TAC portal as of 2026-08-19)
new_rules.notes: Not one of the 36 checklist items; recorded because it is part of the AG's programming/manipulation charge stack.

new_rules.legal_concept: Postal and shipping charges at actual cost
new_rules.atomic_rule: Governmental bodies may add related postal or shipping expenses necessary to transmit the reproduced information to the requestor (actual cost).
new_rules.trigger: Copies are mailed or shipped.
new_rules.source_language: (j) Postal and shipping charges. Governmental bodies may add any related postal or shipping expenses which are necessary to transmit the reproduced information to the requesting party. [...] (9) Postage and shipping charge--Actual cost.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (1 TAC § 70.3 last amended effective February 22, 2007, 32 TexReg 614; verified on the SOS TAC portal as of 2026-08-19)
new_rules.notes: No handling fee, no e-mail delivery charge and no pickup charge is stated. Gov't Code § 552.221(b)(2) makes payment of postage a condition of mailing (TX-9021).

new_rules.legal_concept: Recovery of credit-card transaction fee
new_rules.atomic_rule: A body that accepts credit-card payment for copies and is charged a transaction fee by the card company may recover that fee.
new_rules.trigger: Body accepts payment by credit card and is charged a transaction fee.
new_rules.source_language: (l) Miscellaneous charges: A governmental body that accepts payment by credit card for copies of public information and that is charged a "transaction fee" by the credit card company may recover that fee.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (1 TAC § 70.3 last amended effective February 22, 2007, 32 TexReg 614; verified on the SOS TAC portal as of 2026-08-19)
new_rules.notes: No statute or rule requires an electronic payment method; Handbook 2026 at 56: 'Decisions about method of payment rest with the governmental body.'

new_rules.legal_concept: Inspection deposit capped at 50% of estimate (or bond for full amount)
new_rules.atomic_rule: Where a paper-inspection request qualifies for a deposit or bond, the body may request a bond for the entire estimated amount or a deposit not to exceed 50 percent of the entire estimated amount.
new_rules.trigger: Paper-inspection request qualifies for a deposit or bond under § 70.7(d) / Gov't Code § 552.271(c)-(d).
new_rules.source_language: (e) If a request for the inspection of paper records will qualify for a deposit or a bond as detailed in subsection (d) of this section, a governmental body may request: (1) A bond for the entire estimated amount; or (2) A deposit not to exceed 50 percent of the entire estimated amount.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (1 TAC § 70.7 last amended effective February 22, 2007, 32 TexReg 614; verified on the SOS TAC portal as of 2026-08-19)
new_rules.notes: Applies to INSPECTION of paper records only. For copy requests neither § 552.263 nor § 70.7 states a percentage cap on the deposit (deposit/bond 'for payment of anticipated costs'). Handbook 2026 at 56 confirms the 50% limit is for inspection requests.

new_rules.legal_concept: Failure to provide itemized statement caps collection at $40
new_rules.atomic_rule: A body that fails to provide the required itemized statement of estimated charges may not collect more than $40; the statement must be provided free of charge before copies are made.
new_rules.trigger: Charges will exceed $40 and no itemized statement was provided.
new_rules.source_language: A governmental body that fails to provide the required statement may not collect more than $40. The itemized statement must be provided free of charge and shall contain the following information:
new_rules.effective_status: Current (1 TAC § 70.7 last amended effective February 22, 2007, 32 TexReg 614; verified on the SOS TAC portal as of 2026-08-19)
new_rules.notes: This is a consequence of a missing cost notice, not of a late response. Handbook 2026 at 55: a 'deficient' statement may limit recoverable charges and prevent treating the request as withdrawn.

new_rules.legal_concept: Actual charges over $40 capped at updated estimate or 120% of original
new_rules.atomic_rule: If actual charges exceed $40 they may not exceed the amount in the updated itemized statement, or, if no updated statement was sent, an amount 20 percent or more above the original estimate.
new_rules.trigger: Actual charges for the copy or paper inspection exceed $40.
new_rules.source_language: (d) If the actual charges that a governmental body imposes for a copy of public information, or for inspecting a paper record under Section 552.271, exceeds $40, the charges may not exceed: (1) the amount estimated in the updated itemized statement; or (2) if an updated itemized statement is not sent to the requestor, an amount that exceeds by 20 percent or more the amount estimated in the itemized statement.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Complements TX-0030 (updated statement at >=20% overrun).

new_rules.legal_concept: Charges accrue when copy is available on payment
new_rules.atomic_rule: Charges for a copy accrue at the time the body advises the requestor that the copy is available on payment of the applicable charges.
new_rules.trigger: Body notifies requestor the copy is ready.
new_rules.source_language: (d) Charges for providing a copy of public information are considered to accrue at the time the governmental body advises the requestor that the copy is available on payment of the applicable charges.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Statutory shape: copies are made 'available on payment' — release may be conditioned on payment.

new_rules.legal_concept: Mailing of copies conditioned on payment of postage and accrued charges
new_rules.atomic_rule: The officer complies by mailing copies first-class if the requestor asks for copies and pays the postage and any other applicable charges accrued under Subchapter F.
new_rules.trigger: Requestor asks that copies be mailed.
new_rules.source_language: (2) sending copies of the public information by first class United States mail if the person requesting the information requests that copies be provided and pays the postage and any other applicable charges that the requestor has accrued under Subchapter F.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
new_rules.notes: § 552.221 amended by Acts 2025, 89th Leg., R.S., Ch. 452 (H.B. 4219) (subsections (f)-(g), not this clause).

new_rules.legal_concept: Withdrawal for failure to pay charges or collect records within 60 days
new_rules.atomic_rule: A request is considered withdrawn if the requestor fails to inspect or duplicate the information in the body's offices by the 60th day after it is made available, or fails to pay postage and other accrued charges by the 60th day after being informed of the charges.
new_rules.trigger: 60 days pass after availability notice / charge notice without pickup or payment.
new_rules.clock_spec: 60 calendar-days from the date the information is made available or the date the requestor is informed of the charges
new_rules.source_language: (e) A request is considered to have been withdrawn if the requestor fails to inspect or duplicate the public information in the offices of the governmental body on or before the 60th day after the date the information is made available or fails to pay the postage and any other applicable charges accrued under Subchapter F on or before the 60th day after the date the requestor is informed of the charges.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Days are calendar days ('60th day'). Distinct from the 10-business-day estimate-response withdrawal (TX-0029) and the 10-business-day deposit withdrawal (TX-9024).

new_rules.legal_concept: Request deemed received when deposit or bond is received
new_rules.atomic_rule: For Subchapters F and G, when a deposit or bond is required under § 552.263 the request is considered received on the date the body receives the deposit or bond.
new_rules.trigger: Officer requires a deposit or bond under § 552.263.
new_rules.clock_spec: Statutory clocks (Subchapters F and G) run from the date the deposit or bond is received
new_rules.source_language: (e) For purposes of Subchapters F and G, a request for a copy of public information is considered to have been received by a governmental body on the date the governmental body receives the deposit or bond for payment of anticipated costs or unpaid amounts if the governmental body's officer for public information or the officer's agent requires a deposit or bond in accordance with this section.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Clock effect while a deposit is unpaid: the request is not yet 'received' — production and AG-ruling deadlines start on deposit receipt.

new_rules.legal_concept: Withdrawal for failure to pay deposit within 10 business days
new_rules.atomic_rule: A requestor who fails to make a required deposit or post a required bond before the 10th business day after the date it is required is considered to have withdrawn the request.
new_rules.trigger: 10 business days pass after a deposit/bond is required without payment.
new_rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from the date the deposit or bond is required
new_rules.source_language: (f) A requestor who fails to make a deposit or post a bond required under Subsection (a) before the 10th business day after the date the deposit or bond is required is considered to have withdrawn the request for the copy of the public information that precipitated the requirement of the deposit or bond.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Grace = 10 business days; lapse action = withdrawn.

new_rules.legal_concept: Modified request after deposit demand is a new request
new_rules.atomic_rule: If the requestor modifies the request in response to a deposit or bond requirement, the modified request is a separate request received on the date the written modification is received.
new_rules.trigger: Requestor modifies the request in response to a deposit/bond demand.
new_rules.clock_spec: Clocks restart from receipt of the written modified request
new_rules.source_language: (e-1) If a requestor modifies the request in response to the requirement of a deposit or bond authorized by this section, the modified request is considered a separate request for the purposes of this chapter and is considered received on the date the governmental body receives the written modified request.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)

new_rules.legal_concept: No deposit as down payment for future requests
new_rules.atomic_rule: The officer may not require a deposit or bond as a down payment for copies the requestor may request in the future.
new_rules.trigger: Deposit is sought for anticipated future requests.
new_rules.source_language: (b) The officer for public information or the officer's agent may not require a deposit or bond be paid under Subsection (a) as a down payment for copies of public information that the requestor may request in the future.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)

new_rules.legal_concept: Documentation required before requiring a deposit or bond
new_rules.atomic_rule: The body must fully document the existence and amount of unpaid amounts or anticipated costs before requiring a deposit or bond; the documentation is itself public.
new_rules.trigger: Body intends to require a deposit or bond.
new_rules.source_language: (d) The governmental body must fully document the existence and amount of those unpaid amounts or the amount of any anticipated costs, as applicable, before requiring a deposit or bond under this section. The documentation is subject to required public disclosure under this chapter.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)

new_rules.legal_concept: Same-day requests from one individual may be treated as one request for cost calculation
new_rules.atomic_rule: All requests received in one calendar day from an individual may be treated as a single request for calculating costs; requests from separate individuals on behalf of an organization may not be combined.
new_rules.trigger: Multiple requests from the same individual arrive on one calendar day.
new_rules.source_language: (e) Except as otherwise provided by this subsection, all requests received in one calendar day from an individual may be treated as a single request for purposes of calculating costs under this chapter. A governmental body may not combine multiple requests under this subsection from separate individuals who submit requests on behalf of an organization.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Practical effect: same-day requests may be aggregated to cross the 50-page labor threshold (Handbook 2026 at 52).

new_rules.legal_concept: Repetitious request: free certification of prior production
new_rules.atomic_rule: For information already furnished or made available to the requestor on payment, the body may respond by certifying the prior production (description, dates, no-changes statement, signature); no charge may be imposed for the certification.
new_rules.trigger: Requestor asks again for information previously furnished or made available on payment.
new_rules.source_language: (b) The governmental body shall certify to the requestor that copies of all or part of the requested information, as applicable, were previously furnished to the requestor or made available to the requestor on payment of applicable charges under Subchapter F. [...] (c) A charge may not be imposed for making and furnishing a certification required under Subsection (b).
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
new_rules.notes: The body may instead simply furnish the information again (§ 552.232(a)(1)). Two subsections joined with [...].

new_rules.legal_concept: Written cost estimate within 10 days once personnel-time limit is reached
new_rules.atomic_rule: If cumulative personnel time for a requestor equals or exceeds the body's § 552.275 limit, the body must give a written estimate of total cost (materials, personnel time, overhead) on or before the 10th day after the request; the charge for locating, compiling and producing is set by AG rule.
new_rules.trigger: Requestor's cumulative personnel time reaches the adopted monthly/yearly limit.
new_rules.clock_spec: 10 calendar-days from the date the information was requested (extendable once by written statement, § 552.275(f))
new_rules.source_language: (e) Subject to Subsection (e-1), if in connection with a request for public information, the cumulative amount of personnel time spent complying with requests for public information from the same requestor equals or exceeds the limit established by the governmental body under Subsection (a), the governmental body shall provide the requestor with a written estimate of the total cost, including materials, personnel time, and overhead expenses, necessary to comply with the request. The written estimate must be provided to the requestor on or before the 10th day after the date on which the public information was requested. The amount of this charge relating to the cost of locating, compiling, and producing the public information shall be established by rules prescribed by the attorney general under Sections 552.262(a) and (b).
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Delegation to AG rule followed: 1 TAC § 70.12 (TX-9033).

new_rules.legal_concept: After time limit exceeded, no production until estimate paid; nonpayment = withdrawal
new_rules.atomic_rule: Once a requestor has exceeded the § 552.275 limits and received the written statement, the body need not produce unless the requestor pays the stated amount (or provides ID/payment under (o)) on or before the 10th day after the statement; failure is a withdrawal of the pending request.
new_rules.trigger: Written § 552.275(e) or (o) statement provided to a requestor over the limit.
new_rules.clock_spec: 10 calendar-days from the date the written statement was provided
new_rules.source_language: (g) If a governmental body provides a requestor with a written statement under Subsection (e) or (o) and the time limits prescribed by Subsection (a) regarding the requestor have been exceeded, the governmental body is not required to produce public information for inspection or duplication or to provide copies of public information in response to the requestor's request unless on or before the 10th day after the date the governmental body provided the written statement under that subsection, the requestor submits payment of the amount stated in the written statement provided under Subsection (e) or provides identification or submits payment as required by Subsection (o), as applicable. (h) If the requestor fails or refuses to provide identification or submit payment under Subsection (g), the requestor is considered to have withdrawn the requestor's pending request for public information.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Applies only where the body has adopted § 552.275 limits and the requestor is not exempt under (j)-(l).

new_rules.legal_concept: Unpaid § 552.275 statement on a prior request suspends new requests
new_rules.atomic_rule: Where a requestor has an unpaid § 552.275(e) statement on a previous, non-withdrawn request, the body is not required to locate, compile, produce or estimate for a new request until each unpaid statement is paid or the previous request withdrawn.
new_rules.trigger: New request from a requestor with an unpaid § 552.275(e) statement.
new_rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: until each unpaid statement is paid or the previous request is withdrawn
new_rules.source_language: (e-1) This subsection applies only to a request made by a requestor who has made a previous request to a governmental body that has not been withdrawn, for which the governmental body has located and compiled documents in response, and for which the governmental body has issued a statement under Subsection (e) that remains unpaid on the date the requestor submits the new request. A governmental body is not required to locate, compile, produce, or provide copies of documents or prepare a statement under Subsection (e) in response to a new request described by this subsection until the date the requestor pays each unpaid statement issued under Subsection (e) in connection with a previous request or withdraws the previous request to which the statement applies.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Added by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033).

new_rules.legal_concept: Method for § 552.275 charges and time excluded from the personnel-time count
new_rules.atomic_rule: Charges under § 552.275 are calculated with the § 70.3(c)-(e) methods; when counting a requestor's personnel time the body may not include time spent interpreting/scoping or clarifying the request, comparing records from different sources, determining exceptions, preparing § 552.301/.303/.305 materials, reorganizing records to accepted management practices, or staff training.
new_rules.trigger: Body applies a § 552.275 personnel-time limit.
new_rules.source_language: (a) A governmental body shall utilize the methods established in 1 TAC §70.3(c) - (e) when calculating allowable charges under Section 552.275 of the Texas Government Code. (b) When calculating the amount of time spent complying with an individual's public information request(s) pursuant to Section 552.275 of the Texas Government Code, a governmental body may not include time spent on: (1) Determining the meaning and/or scope of the request(s); (2) Requesting a clarification from the requestor; (3) Comparing records gathered from different sources; (4) Determining which exceptions to disclosure under Chapter 552 of the Texas Government Code, if any, may apply to information that is responsive to the request(s); (5) Preparing the information and/or correspondence required under Sections 552.301, 552.303, and 552.305 of the Government Code; (6) Reordering, reorganizing, or in any other way bringing information into compliance with well established and generally accepted information management practices; or (7) Providing instruction to, or learning by, employees or agents of the governmental body of new practices, rules, and/or procedures, including the management of electronic records.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (adopted effective September 5, 2007, 32 TexReg 5653; verified on the SOS TAC portal as of 2026-08-19)
new_rules.notes: Instrument delegated by Gov't Code § 552.275(e).

new_rules.legal_concept: Requestors exempt from § 552.275 personnel-time limits
new_rules.atomic_rule: § 552.275 limits do not apply to a requestor who is a working journalist/news-media gatherer (or abstract-plant creator), an elected official of the U.S., the state or a political subdivision, or a representative of a publicly funded 501(c)(3) legal-services organization.
new_rules.trigger: Requestor falls in one of the (j)-(l) classes.
new_rules.source_language: (j) This section does not apply if the requestor is an individual who, for a substantial portion of the individual's livelihood or for substantial financial gain, gathers, compiles, prepares, collects, photographs, records, writes, edits, reports, investigates, processes, or publishes news or information for and is seeking the information for: (1) dissemination by a news medium or communication service provider, including: (A) an individual who supervises or assists in gathering, preparing, and disseminating the news or information; or (B) an individual who is or was a journalist, scholar, or researcher employed by an institution of higher education at the time the person made the request for information; or (2) creation or maintenance of an abstract plant as described by Section 2501.004, Insurance Code. (k) This section does not apply if the requestor is an elected official of the United States, this state, or a political subdivision of this state. (l) This section does not apply if the requestor is a representative of a publicly funded legal services organization that is exempt from federal income taxation under Section 501(a), Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, by being listed as an exempt entity under Section 501(c)(3) of that code.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Requestor-class branch the engine must express if a city adopts § 552.275 limits.

new_rules.legal_concept: No charge for inspecting paper records except photocopy of redacted pages
new_rules.atomic_rule: If no copy is requested, no charge may be imposed for making paper records available for inspection, except the cost of photocopying a page from which confidential information must be edited (and the personnel-cost cases in § 552.271(c)-(d)).
new_rules.trigger: Requestor asks to inspect (not copy) paper records.
new_rules.source_language: (a) If the requestor does not request a copy of public information, a charge may not be imposed for making available for inspection any public information that exists in a paper record, except as provided by this section. (b) If a requested page contains confidential information that must be edited from the record before the information can be made available for inspection, the governmental body may charge for the cost of making a photocopy of the page from which confidential information must be edited. No charge other than the cost of the photocopy may be imposed under this subsection.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)

new_rules.legal_concept: Personnel costs for paper inspection only for old/voluminous records over an hours threshold
new_rules.atomic_rule: The officer may require payment, deposit or bond for anticipated personnel costs of preparing paper records for inspection only if the records are older than five years or fill six or more archival boxes AND more than five hours are estimated (bodies with fewer than 16 full-time employees: older than three years or three or more boxes AND more than two hours).
new_rules.trigger: Inspection request for old or voluminous paper records.
new_rules.source_language: (c) Except as provided by Subsection (d), an officer for public information or the officer's agent may require a requestor to pay, or to make a deposit or post a bond for the payment of, anticipated personnel costs for making available for inspection public information that exists in paper records only if: (1) the public information specifically requested by the requestor: (A) is older than five years; or (B) completely fills, or when assembled will completely fill, six or more archival boxes; and (2) the officer for public information or the officer's agent estimates that more than five hours will be required to make the public information available for inspection. (d) If the governmental body has fewer than 16 full-time employees, the payment, the deposit, or the bond authorized by Subsection (c) may be required only if: (1) the public information specifically requested by the requestor: (A) is older than three years; or (B) completely fills, or when assembled will completely fill, three or more archival boxes; and (2) the officer for public information or the officer's agent estimates that more than two hours will be required to make the public information available for inspection.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033). Overhead not allowed on inspection (Handbook 2026 at 53). 'Archival box' defined at 1 TAC § 70.2(10).

new_rules.legal_concept: No charge for electronic inspection unless programming/manipulation; estimate first
new_rules.atomic_rule: For inspection of electronic information not available online, no charge may be imposed unless programming or manipulation of data is required, in which case the body must notify the requestor before assembling and give an estimate of charges.
new_rules.trigger: Request to inspect electronic information not directly available online.
new_rules.source_language: (a) In response to a request to inspect information that exists in an electronic medium and that is not available directly on-line to the requestor, a charge may not be imposed for access to the information, unless complying with the request will require programming or manipulation of data. If programming or manipulation of data is required, the governmental body shall notify the requestor before assembling the information and provide the requestor with an estimate of charges that will be imposed to make the information available. A charge under this section must be assessed in accordance with this subchapter.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)

new_rules.legal_concept: Programming/manipulation statement: 20-day notice, 30-day requestor election, else withdrawn
new_rules.atomic_rule: If a request requires programming or manipulation of data and is infeasible/interfering or available only at a cost covering that work, the body must send a written statement (form available, contracts needed, estimated cost per AG rules, time) within 20 days (+10 with notice); the requestor has 30 days to elect in writing or the request is withdrawn.
new_rules.trigger: Response requires programming or manipulation of data and § 552.231(a)(2) applies.
new_rules.clock_spec: 20 calendar-days from receipt of request for the statement (+10 with written notice); 30 days for the requestor's written election, else withdrawn (terminal)
new_rules.source_language: (4) a statement of the estimated cost of providing the information in the requested form, as determined in accordance with the rules established by the attorney general under Section 552.262; [...] (c) The governmental body shall provide the written statement to the requestor within 20 days after the date of the governmental body's receipt of the request. The governmental body has an additional 10 days to provide the statement if the governmental body gives written notice to the requestor, within 20 days after the date of receipt of the request, that the additional time is needed. (d) On providing the written statement to the requestor as required by this section, the governmental body does not have any further obligation to provide the information in the requested form or in the form in which it is available unless within 30 days the requestor states in writing to the governmental body that the requestor: (1) wants the governmental body to provide the information in the requested form according to the cost and time parameters set out in the statement or according to other terms to which the requestor and the governmental body agree; or (2) wants the information in the form in which it is available. (d-1) If a requestor does not make a timely written statement under Subsection (d), the requestor is considered to have withdrawn the request for information.

new_rules.legal_concept: Body-worn-camera recording copy fee: $10 per recording + $1 per full minute
new_rules.atomic_rule: The charge for a copy of a body worn camera recording from a law enforcement agency is $10.00 per responsive recording plus $1.00 per full minute of responsive video/audio if identical information has not already been obtained by a member of the public; the agency may waive or reduce it in the public interest and may not charge if the requestor is not permitted to obtain the copy.
new_rules.trigger: Request is for a copy of a body worn camera recording held by a law enforcement agency.
new_rules.source_language: (b) The charge for obtaining a copy of a body worn camera recording shall be: (1) $10.00 per recording responsive to the request for information; and (2) $1.00 per full minute of body worn camera video or audio footage responsive to the request for information, if identical information has not already been obtained by a member of the public in response to a request for information. (c) A law enforcement agency may provide a copy without charge, or at a reduced charge, if the agency determines waiver or reduction of the charge is in the public interest. (d) If the requestor is not permitted to obtain a copy of a requested body worn camera recording under §1701.661 of the Government Code or an exception in the Public Information Act, Chapter 552 of the Government Code, the law enforcement agency may not charge the requestor under this section.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (adopted effective November 24, 2016, 41 TexReg 9099; verified on the SOS TAC portal as of 2026-08-19). Rule text still cites Occ. Code § 1701.661, recodified as Code Crim. Proc. art. 2B.0112 eff. Jan. 1, 2025
new_rules.notes: Applies to law enforcement agencies (municipal police departments included). § 70.13(a)(1): 'no fee for obtaining a copy of a body worn camera recording from a law enforcement agency may be charged unless authorized by this section'; other portions of a request fall under § 70.3. Whether the § 552.262(a) 25% variance applies to this schedule is not addressed — flag.

new_rules.legal_concept: AG sets the body-worn-camera recording fee
new_rules.atomic_rule: The attorney general shall set a proposed fee for copies of body worn camera recordings sufficient to cover the cost of reviewing and making the recording; the agency may waive or reduce it in the public interest.
new_rules.trigger: Request for a copy of a body worn camera recording.
new_rules.source_language: (g) The attorney general shall set a proposed fee to be charged to members of the public who seek to obtain a copy of a recording under this article in an amount sufficient to cover the cost of reviewing and making the recording. A law enforcement agency may provide a copy without charge or at a reduced charge if the agency determines that waiver or reduction of the charge is in the public interest.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Added by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 765 (H.B. 4504), eff. January 1, 2025; formerly Occ. Code § 1701.661(f))
new_rules.notes: Delegation followed to 1 TAC § 70.13 (TX-9039).

new_rules.legal_concept: No inquiry into the requestor's purpose
new_rules.atomic_rule: The officer may not make any inquiry of a requestor except to establish identification (or the § 552.222(b)-(c-1) cases), and even when discussing narrowing a large request may not inquire into the purpose for which the information will be used.
new_rules.trigger: Any request.
new_rules.source_language: (a) The officer for public information and the officer's agent may not make an inquiry of a requestor except to establish proper identification or except as provided by Subsection (b), (c), or (c-1). (b) If what information is requested is unclear to the governmental body, the governmental body may ask the requestor to clarify the request. If a large amount of information has been requested, the governmental body may discuss with the requestor how the scope of a request might be narrowed, but the governmental body may not inquire into the purpose for which information will be used.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Bears on fee items: no commercial-purpose schedule and no purpose statement can be required for a waiver. Uses the shared V2 eligibility key.

new_rules.legal_concept: Municipal court clerk copies charged per municipal ordinance
new_rules.atomic_rule: The charge for a copy made by a municipal court clerk is the charge provided by municipal ordinance.
new_rules.trigger: Copy is made by a municipal court clerk.
new_rules.source_language: Sec. 552.266. CHARGE FOR COPY OF PUBLIC INFORMATION PROVIDED BY MUNICIPAL COURT CLERK. The charge for providing a copy made by a municipal court clerk shall be the charge provided by municipal ordinance.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)

new_rules.legal_concept: Free signed statement of labor time on request
new_rules.atomic_rule: If a copy charge includes labor, the requestor may require a signed written statement of the time required to produce and provide the copy; no charge may be imposed for the statement.
new_rules.trigger: Charge includes labor and requestor asks for the time statement.
new_rules.source_language: (b) If the charge for providing a copy of public information includes costs of labor, the requestor may require the governmental body's officer for public information or the officer's agent to provide the requestor with a written statement as to the amount of time that was required to produce and provide the copy. The statement must be signed by the officer for public information or the officer's agent and the officer's or the agent's name must be typed or legibly printed below the signature. A charge may not be imposed for providing the written statement to the requestor.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Also restated at 1 TAC § 70.3(c)(3), (d)(5).

new_rules.legal_concept: Overcharge complaint to the Attorney General; 10-business-day response; adjustment
new_rules.atomic_rule: A person who believes they were overcharged may complain in writing to the AG; the body must answer the AG's written questions within 10 business days of receipt and, if the AG finds an overcharge, promptly adjust its charges per the determination.
new_rules.trigger: Requestor files an overcharge complaint with the AG.
new_rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from receipt of the AG's written questions (body's response)
new_rules.source_language: (a) A person who believes the person has been overcharged for being provided with a copy of public information may complain to the attorney general in writing of the alleged overcharge, setting forth the reasons why the person believes the charges are excessive. The attorney general shall review the complaint and make a determination in writing as to the appropriate charge for providing the copy of the requested information. The governmental body shall respond to the attorney general to any written questions asked of the governmental body by the attorney general regarding the charges for providing the copy of the public information. The response must be made to the attorney general within 10 business days after the date the questions are received by the governmental body. If the attorney general determines that a governmental body has overcharged for providing the copy of requested public information, the governmental body shall promptly adjust its charges in accordance with the determination of the attorney general.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Gov't Code ch. 552 as codified through the 89th Leg., R.S. and 2nd C.S. (2025); Subchapter F last amended by Acts 2023, 88th Leg., R.S., Ch. 847 (H.B. 3033), eff. Sept. 1, 2023)
new_rules.notes: 1 TAC § 70.8(b)(3): complaint must reach the AG within 10 business days after the person knows of the alleged overcharge. Treble-damages remedy in § 552.269(b) excluded (remedy amount).

new_rules.legal_concept: Governmental bodies must use AG charges unless a listed exception applies
new_rules.atomic_rule: Governmental bodies must use the charges established by 1 TAC ch. 70 unless other law sets charges for specific records, they are a non-state body within a 25 percent variance above the AG charges, they obtain an exemption, or they waive/reduce under § 552.267.
new_rules.trigger: Body sets charges for copies.
new_rules.source_language: (b) Governmental bodies must use the charges established by these rules, unless: (1) Other law provides for charges for specific kinds of public information; (2) They are a governmental body other than a state agency, and their charges are within a 25 percent variance above the charges established by the Attorney General; (3) They request and receive an exemption because their actual costs are higher; or (4) In accordance with Chapter 552 of the Texas Government Code (also known as the Public Information Act), the governmental body may grant a waiver or reduction for charges for providing copies of public information pursuant to §552.267 of the Texas Government Code.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (1 TAC § 70.1 last amended effective February 22, 2007, 32 TexReg 614; verified on the SOS TAC portal as of 2026-08-19)
new_rules.notes: The municipal-scope key: AG figures are a baseline for cities with a 25% variance ceiling.

new_rules.legal_concept: Non-state bodies must obtain an exemption before exceeding AG charges by more than 25%
new_rules.atomic_rule: Governmental bodies other than state agencies must request an exemption before recovering costs more than 25% higher than the AG-established charges; the AG decides within 90 days and lists exempt bodies annually in the Texas Register.
new_rules.trigger: City wants to charge more than 25% above an AG-established amount.
new_rules.source_language: (c) Governmental bodies, other than agencies of the state, must request an exemption before seeking to recover costs that are more than 25% higher than the charges established by these rules. [...] (h) All determinations to grant or deny a request for exemption shall be completed promptly, but shall not exceed 90 days from receipt of the request by the Attorney General.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (1 TAC § 70.4 last amended effective February 22, 2007, 32 TexReg 614; verified on the SOS TAC portal as of 2026-08-19)

new_rules.legal_concept: No sales tax on public-information charges
new_rules.atomic_rule: Sales tax shall not be added to charges for public information.
new_rules.trigger: Any charge for public information.
new_rules.source_language: (k) Sales tax. Pursuant to Office of the Comptroller of Public Accounts' rules sales tax shall not be added on charges for public information (34 TAC, Part 1, Chapter 3, Subchapter O, §3.341 and §3.342).

new_rules.legal_concept: Miscellaneous supplies at actual cost
new_rules.atomic_rule: The actual cost of miscellaneous supplies (labels, boxes, etc.) used to produce the information may be added to the total charge.
new_rules.trigger: Supplies are consumed producing the copies.
new_rules.source_language: (i) Miscellaneous supplies. The actual cost of miscellaneous supplies, such as labels, boxes, and other supplies used to produce the requested information, may be added to the total charge for public information.

new_rules.legal_concept: Remote document retrieval: contractor fee recoverable, no double labor
new_rules.atomic_rule: Costs of retrieving records from remote storage may be recovered (actual cost) for requests that qualify for labor charges; where a commercial storage contractor charges to locate/retrieve/return records, no additional labor is added for the contractor's time, but labor is allowed for searching delivered boxes.
new_rules.trigger: Records are held in remote storage.
new_rules.source_language: (1) [...] To the extent that the retrieval of documents results in a charge to comply with a request, it is permissible to recover costs of such services for requests that qualify for labor charges under current law. (2) If a governmental body has a contract with a commercial records storage company, whereby the private company charges a fee to locate, retrieve, deliver, and return to storage the needed record(s), no additional labor charge shall be factored in for time spent locating documents at the storage location by the private company's personnel. If after delivery to the governmental body, the boxes must still be searched for records that are responsive to the request, a labor charge is allowed according to subsection (d)(1) of this section.

applicability_notes: Texas runs ONE statutory regime for all governmental bodies (Gov't Code ch. 552 applies to municipalities, counties, districts and state agencies alike); the split is inside § 552.262(a): state agencies must charge the AG-established amounts, while 'a governmental body, other than an agency of state government' may set its own charges up to 25 percent above the AG amount without an exemption. Every § 70.3 figure is therefore recorded as a CEILING for municipalities (AG rate | AG rate + 25%), never as a fixed value.

The +25% municipal figures ($.125/page, $18.75/hr, $35.625/hr, $.625 oversize, $1.25 CD, $3.75 DVD) are arithmetic derivations of two verbatim numbers, not printed figures; a city may go higher only with a written AG exemption (1 TAC § 70.4; exempt bodies published annually in the Texas Register).
Whether the 25% variance applies to the 20% overhead percentage and to the § 70.13 body-worn-camera schedule is not addressed in ch. 70 or the Handbook — flagged for manual verification.

Statutory thresholds and clocks ($40 statement, 20% update, $100/$50 deposit by FTE count, >$100 prior unpaid, 10 business days, 60 days, 36/15-hour floors) apply to all governmental bodies and are not subject to the 25% variance.
The § 552.263(a) deposit thresholds and § 552.271(c)-(d) inspection thresholds turn on the body's full-time-employee count (more than 15 vs fewer than 16); a city's configuration needs its FTE class.
Municipal court clerk copies are priced by municipal ordinance (§ 552.266); district/county clerk copies by other statutes (§ 552.265) — record-specific carve-outs from the AG schedule.
Body-worn-camera recording fees (1 TAC § 70.13) bind law enforcement agencies, which include municipal police departments; other municipal departments' A/V copies fall under § 70.3.
material_negatives: No color-copy rate; no volume-graduated per-page bands; no free-page allowance; no per-request free labor hours; no labor billing increment or rounding rule; no estimate validity period; no percentage cap on deposits for COPY requests (only for paper-inspection deposits); no minimum fee; no fixed de-minimis dollar amount; no certification/certified-copy charge in the PIA or AG rules; no commercial-purpose schedule (purpose inquiry is prohibited); no fee forfeiture for a late response; no mandate to offer electronic payment; no e-mail delivery or handling charge; no per-minute or free-minute construct for general (non-body-cam) audio/video.
